summary: Unknown command: onCommand and * activation are both awaited, then _tryExecuteCommand rejects with "command '<id>' not found" (commandService.ts:78-96). Outcome and path are reproduced. The activationEventIsDone short-circuit and the race against command registration are not modeled.

Last-to-first when matching and fall-through are reproduced (Ctrl+W: closeGroup vs closeActiveEditor; editorTextFocus none vs found). Path is wrong: the context comes from the request, not contextKeyService.getContext; workbench-shell commands bypass ICommandService.executeCommand; when supports only k or !k, so closeGroup's and() is a synthetic key.

Only showCommands -> quickAccess.show('>') is modeled. Listing commands (getCommandPicks) and pick accept -> history push -> ICommandService.executeCommand (platform commandsQuickAccess.ts:303-323) have no entity.

Corrected: onExit backs up with no prompt only when the LAST window closes on Windows or Linux; with other windows open (or macOS) the user is prompted (workingCopyBackupTracker.ts:162-209). The close path is reproduced end to end for both cases. On restart, a backup resolves the model dirty, but restoreBackups (reopening editors) is not modeled, and close->restart cannot be chained in one scenario.
Dirty editor close: showSaveConfirm, then Cancel vetoes and the editor and dirty model stay (editorGroupView.ts:1738-1883). Path and outcome are reproduced; the Save and Don't Save controls pass.

Refined: layers merge default<application<user<workspace<folder(resource), then [lang] override applies to the consolidated model, so a user [typescript] beats a general workspace value (configurationModels.ts:1033-1085). The model handles policy>workspace>user>default but ignores override_identifier and resource and has no folder layer, so it returns the wrong value.

The existing editor is activated with is_new false and no new editor entry. Nuance: with several groups and revealIfOpen=false, a second editor opens in the active group but shares the model. The model's open path never resolves the text file model (no editor pane -> TextFileEditorModelManager.resolve), so 'no second model' holds only vacuously.
